title: Combining and Forward-Carrying Overlapping Wellbore Surveys: An Open Implementation Demonstrated on Public Volve Data
description: When two independent surveys overlap the same interval of a wellbore - most commonly an MWD survey and a gyroscopic survey - the industry routinely keeps one and discards the other. This paper provides an open, validated implementation (welleng) of two operations, demonstrated end-to-end on the public Volve dataset. First, it combines overlapping surveys with the best linear unbiased estimator (BLUE), evaluated on the analytical arc-faithful interior covariance (the Rodrigues form of minimum-curvature interpolation, after Sawaryn and Thorogood 2005) so the result is continuous in measured depth. Second, it carries the calibration forward: where a gyro overlaps the upper part of an MWD run, the gyro constrains the MWD's systematic (magnetic) error - including terms a magnetic survey cannot observe from its own data - and, because that systematic realisation persists down-hole, the constraint reduces the MWD covariance in the deeper, gyro-free section. On Volve well F-4 the combination reduces the vertical 1-sigma by about a factor of 1.4 over the overlap; carrying the gyro-observed declination forward reduces the deep MWD-only lateral 1-sigma unconditionally, and by roughly a factor of two when the same MWD tool is reused below. Neither method is novel - both adopt established estimation theory - so the contribution is the open implementation, the analytical/continuous formulation, and the quantified demonstration on public field data. The implementation is validated against an independent stacked generalized-least-squares oracle to a relative tolerance of 1e-8, against a Monte-Carlo oracle, and reproduces the ~29% equal-accuracy reduction reported by Bang (2019, SPE-195621). Use requires citation of this work and welleng. Version 1.1 adds a section on reconstructing the fused position path as a minimum-curvature (measured depth, inclination, azimuth) survey listing via a single-pass analytical (reflection) inverse - measured depth held exact, drawable by conventional survey software - presented as a concept pending field validation, with its interval/curvature bound quantified.
